Given this log’s legend, which rock is this patch?

SAMPLE2 leads this benchmark: fixed-seed sampling targets 60 intervals per family, covers as many logs as possible, caps each log at 15, and balances available tiers and interval-height strata. It excludes log06, intervals under 16 rows and intervals within 30 rows of either column edge. MC761 has only three logs, so its maximum is 45. Classifiers receive the complete native-scale interval.

Reference readers independently label sheets of up to eight patches from one log, with 40 rows of context and that log’s original legend. Only identical, non-unknown Sol (high) and Terra (medium) answers are retained. Terra classification uses a fixed 25% per-family subsample (rounded down). Agreement favours easier patches and can retain shared mistakes; Terra is not independent of these reference labels.

TRUE retains the organisers’ 17 log06 patches. CONSENSUS retains the original window-based Sol/Terra agreements. These older sources use central crops up to 160 rows, a 12-row minimum and a 40-patch window cap. Each source is scored separately.

Hardware: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4080 Laptop GPU. All scores are per interval patch, not per pixel row or depth. Small samples and repeated patterns within a single log limit generalisation.

Interpretation: nearest-colour methods discard hatch structure, so monochrome patterns can tie. FFT compares directional frequency and ink density; embeddings compare learned visual similarity. Fine-grained adjacent legend colours, scan colour shifts, narrow/full-width mixtures and OCR label or swatch errors can hurt all methods. The paired examples show errors; these mechanisms are hypotheses rather than causal measurements.

The best local classifier and a single top-two probability margin threshold are selected on log06 TRUE only: maximise top-1, break ties by fewer JEV calls. JEV choice is fixed in advance. The policy is frozen for CONSENSUS. Hybrid scores use cached standalone outputs and incur no extra benchmark requests; latency and calls estimate a sequential deployment. Missing JEV responses retain the local answer. Threshold transfer between families is unvalidated.

Calls, latency and memory

Unknown: no verified JEV tariff or Terra account billing; calls and reported tokens are recorded.

Actual API requests: {"jev_choice": 89, "jev_gallery": 88, "terra": 22}. Reported token usage: {"jev_choice": {"input_tokens": 209303, "output_tokens": 14750}, "jev_gallery": {"input_tokens": 189767, "output_tokens": 14744}, "terra": {"input_tokens": 0, "output_tokens": 0}}. Local classifiers have no paid API calls; electricity/hardware costs are not measured.

Includes model loading, swatch embedding, CNN training and inference amortized over window patches; input/legend preparation excluded. API cached reruns retain original request latency/calls; calls.jsonl separately records actual requests and cache hits. Hybrid is simulated from cached standalone outputs and makes no additional requests.

Unavailable API timings are time spent on failed attempts and skipped requests, not measured model inference latency. CLI invocations count toward the Terra cap even when startup fails; successful remote requests and actual charges cannot be inferred from those invocation counts.

Sampled process RSS including children at 30ms; GPU is peak PyTorch reserved allocator memory, includes already-resident context/models and excludes remote compute.

What this measures

Classifiers receive interval crops with boundaries already supplied. This does not measure segmentation, boundary detection or depth calibration. No real-image training labels are used by the local models: the CNN is trained only on synthetic augmentations of this log’s own swatches, with S7’s 20-second training limit. DINOv2 uses cosine similarity; SigLIP uses S6’s equal visual/text score blend. Colour uses S1’s dominant colour in Lab; FFT uses S11’s hatch and colour descriptor over tiles spanning the patch.

JEV choice uses original legend rock-entry strips beside one query patch. JEV gallery uses labelled cropped swatches beside the same patch. Each makes one choice question and ranks the returned probabilities, with no network retries. When the parser finds no rocks, VLMs use vocab.json and the original legend crop; swatch-based local methods are unavailable. Terra uses gpt-6.1-terra at low effort, eight numbered patches per image, at most 60 invocations in total. Every API response and failure is cached; repeated transport failures stop further calls.

Patch-weighted top1/top3; missing predictions count wrong when partial coverage exists; entirely unavailable cells are NA. Macro-F1 uses classes present in truth. Local probabilities are softmax similarity scores, Terra probabilities self-reported; neither is calibrated. Ties use legend order. Top-1 intervals are 95% Wilson intervals over eligible patches (unavailable predictions count wrong); they do not account for within-log correlation. SAMPLE2 Terra uses a deterministic 25% per-family subset, rounded down; its n and log coverage refer only to that subset. Family choice requires the best top1 Wilson lower bound to exceed the runner-up point estimate; otherwise tie. This rule is descriptive, not a paired significance test.

TRUE is only one monochrome family, with repeated hatch motifs and 17 correlated intervals. The organisers’ “Sandstone” is matched to the legend’s “Sand and Sandstone” via the harness scorer alias. CONSENSUS is machine agreement, not an independent geologist’s ground truth; agreement filtering favours easier rows and can preserve shared model mistakes. The vocabulary comes from parsed legend entries, whose OCR can be wrong. Labels outside the legend vocabulary and short intervals are excluded and logged. Stratification changes natural class prevalence. Top-3 can be forgiving in small vocabularies; macro-F1 averages classes observed in truth. The hybrid’s TRUE score is fitted and optimistic. No result establishes accuracy on unseen wells.
